mechanism_narrative: EGFR (RTK) and IL6ST (gp130, cytokine receptor) are both expressed in aged skeletal muscle MuSC and FB compartments. The rigid_helix_20 linker (~30 Å) forces EGFR's kinase domain into proximity with IL6ST's JAK-associated intracellular domain. EGFR's tyrosine kinase transphosphorylates IL6ST's cytoplasmic tyrosines, creating docking sites for GRB2-SHC1 (MAPK), PIK3R1 (PI3K/AKT), and STAT3 (JAK/STAT). PLCG1/2 are sterically excluded because the EGFR-IL6ST co-cluster geometry cannot accommodate PLCγ's two SH2 domains bridging both receptors simultaneously. FRS2/3 and GAB1/2 are also excluded as they require specific phosphotyrosine motifs on FGFR-family or cytokine receptors that EGFR does not provide. The biased output is MAPK+PI3K+STAT3 activation without PLCγ/Ca²⁺ signaling — a rejuvenating profile that upregulates muscle structural genes (ACTA2, MYL9, MYH11) and downregulates aged IEGs (EGR1, FOS, JUN, IL32).
